questions.prompt: Why does the design retrieve ~500 candidates before ranking, instead of ranking all 10 million videos?

options.text: The ranking model can only output 500 scores
Scoring 10 million videos with a heavy model on every request would take far too long and cost far too much

questions.explanation: A cheap retrieval stage narrows the catalog so the expensive ranking model only scores a few hundred items within the latency budget.

questions.prompt: Why is click-through rate alone a poor ranking objective?

options.text: It rewards clickbait: videos people click but quickly abandon or dislike

questions.explanation: Combining play probability with expected watch time, likes and dismissals better reflects whether viewers were satisfied.

questions.prompt: A video was uploaded 20 minutes ago and has no watches. How can it still be retrieved?

options.text: It can't until it has enough watches
The video tower embeds it from content and metadata, and it's added to the index without retraining
By retraining the whole model every 20 minutes

questions.explanation: Content-based item features let the tower place a brand-new video near viewers who like similar content.

questions.prompt: Which practices counter the feedback loop where the system only learns about what it already shows?

options.text: Reserve a small share of slots for exploration and log how items were chosen
Train only on the top-ranked item per request

questions.explanation: Exploration and position modelling give the model evidence about items it would otherwise never show; diversity keeps recommendations from narrowing. Training only on top items makes the loop worse.

questions.prompt: After retraining both towers, recommendations suddenly become random. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The new user tower was deployed, but the index still holds embeddings from the old video tower
The ANN index ran out of memory

questions.explanation: Embeddings from different tower versions live in different spaces. Deploy the user tower and the re-embedded index together as one version.
